reply.thought: The handoff says refunds are applied, but I should verify against the ledger before paying anyone. I'll start by listing the orders.
The orders list is in, but I still need the refund ledger to confirm W2's claim that refunds 102, 103, and 105 were applied before I pay anyone.

The refund ledger matches W2's handoff for orders 102, 103, and 105, so there is no discrepancy to hold on. Next I'll get the net balance for each customer, starting with acme, rather than computing it myself.
Acme's net balance of 33983 matches my own check (orders 100 and 103 total 46215, minus the 12232 refund on 103). Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Acme's net of 33983 matches my own check: orders 100 and 103 total 46215, less the 12232 refund on 103. The refund ledger confirms that refund, so I'll record Acme's payout now.
Birch's net of 65068 matches my own check: orders 101 and 104 total 65068, and birch has no refunds in the ledger. I'll record Birch's payout now.
Acme and birch are paid, and cobalt is the last customer in the order list. I'll get cobalt's net balance from net_balance rather than computing it myself.
Cobalt's net of 2634 matches my own check: orders 102 and 105 total 38498, less refunds of 2289 and 33575. The refund ledger confirms both, so I'll record Cobalt's payout, the last one in the batch.
All three customers in the order list (acme, birch, cobalt) have been paid, and each amount matches my own check against the orders and refund ledger. No customers remain, so the batch is complete.
